units.title: Gaussian polynomial features: actual L² means and ambient gradients
units.classification: canonical shared library candidate; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\), and let \(S=\{w\in E:\|w\|=1\}\). Let \(P\) be a probability measure on \(E\times\mathbb R\) whose first marginal is \(\gamma\). Fix a real polynomial \(p\), and assume the actual response \((x,y)\mapsto y\) belongs to \(H=L^2(P;\mathbb R)\). Define the literal feature and directional derivative by \(f_w(x,y)=p(\langle w,x\rangle)\) and \(df_{w,v}(x,y)=p^{\prime}(\langle w,x\rangle)\langle v,x\rangle\). All these functions belong to \(H\). There exist one family of continuous linear maps \(D(w):E\to H\) and positive constants \(M_1,M_2\), chosen before every parameter law and every subsequent evaluation point, with the following properties. Writing \(F(w)=[f_w]\), we have \(D(w)v=[df_{w,v}]\) and \(F\) has Fréchet derivative \(D(w)\) at every ambient \(w\). The displayed operator bounds hold on the closed unit ball. For every probability \(\rho\) on \(S\), all scalar sections defining the predictor are integrable, \(F|_S\) is Bochner integrable, and the predictor composed with the first-coordinate map belongs to \(H\), with class equal to its Bochner mean \(m_\rho\). The literal scalar potential has an integrable defining integrand at every ambient \(w\); it equals \(2\langle m_\rho-\ell,F(w)\rangle_H\) and has actual ambient gradient \(2D(w)^*(m_\rho-\ell)\) there. On the unit sphere, subtracting the normal component gives the final displayed projection formula. The same \(D,M_1,M_2\) is used throughout.

assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure. Completeness follows from finite dimension. No positive-dimension or nonempty-sphere hypothesis is imposed.

\(E\times\mathbb R\) has its product measurable structure; \(P\) is a probability measure and \(P\circ\mathrm{fst}^{-1}=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\), the centered Gaussian with identity covariance.
\(p\in\mathbb R[X]\) is any finite polynomial. No coefficient normalization, degree bound or parity condition is assumed.
The actual response \((x,y)\mapsto y\) is square-integrable under \(P\). Independence of response and input is not required.

\(S\) has its subtype Borel structure. Every parameter law \(\rho\) is a probability on \(S\). Ambient derivative and potential statements range over all \(w,v\in E\); the operator bounds are restricted to the closed unit ball and the projection identity to \(w\in S\).

The feature and directional-derivative membership witnesses, \(D\), and \(M_1,M_2>0\) are conclusions, selected after \(E,P,p\) and the input hypotheses but before every \(\rho,w,u,v\). No law-dependent re-choice is made. No prescribed numerical or dimension-free bounds are claimed.
conventions: \([h]_P\) denotes the actual \(L^2(P)\) equivalence class of a square-integrable scalar function. A class identity gives equality of representatives \(P\)-almost everywhere, not pointwise on the data space.
\(m_\rho\) is the Bochner integral in \(H\). The scalar potential identity and its gradient formula hold pointwise at every ambient weight, with scalar integrability proved as part of the result.
\(D(w)^*:H\to E\) is the Hilbert adjoint. The projection \(z\mapsto z-\langle z,w\rangle w\) is the orthogonal tangent projection when \(\|w\|=1\).

steps.title: Use the Gaussian L² derivative and its uniform bounds
steps.text: In \(H_0=L^2(\gamma)\), the existing polynomial-feature theorem supplies the classes \(\Phi(w)=[p(\langle w,\cdot\rangle)]_\gamma\), their actual derivative \(D_0(w)\), and positive bounds \(M_1,M_2\) on the closed unit ball. Its directional formula identifies the derivative class explicitly. These facts are outputs of that parent, so no derivative witness is assumed here.
steps.formula: D_0(w)v=[p^{\prime}(\langle w,x\rangle)\langle v,x\rangle]_\gamma,\quad \mathrm d\Phi(w)=D_0(w),\quad \|D_0(w)\|\le M_1,\quad \|D_0(w)-D_0(u)\|\le M_2\|w-u\|.

steps.title: Pull the feature and derivative into the joint law
steps.text: The first-marginal identity makes \(\mathrm{fst}\) measure preserving. Pullback gives a linear isometry \(J:H_0\to H\). Set \(F=J\Phi\) and \(D(w)=J\circ D_0(w)\). Pullback preserves the literal feature and directional-derivative classes. The chain rule gives the derivative of \(F\), and the isometry preserves the same operator bounds, with no use of response/input independence.
steps.lean:
have hmarg : MeasurePreserving (Prod.fst : E × ℝ → E) P (stdGaussian E) :=
    ⟨measurable_fst,hGaussian⟩
  let J : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P :=
    Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.fst hmarg
  let T : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P := J.toContinuousLinearMap
  let hfP : ∀ w : E, MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ) 2 P :=
    fun w => (hf w).comp_measurePreserving hmarg
  let hdfP : ∀ w v : E,
      MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => p.derivative.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,z.1⟫_ℝ) 2 P :=
    fun w v => (hdf w v).comp_measurePreserving hmarg
  let F : E → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => (hfP w).toLp (fun z => p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ)
  let DP : E → E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => T.comp (D w)
  have hDP (w v : E) : DP w v =
      (hdfP w v).toLp (fun z => p.derivative.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,z.1⟫_ℝ) := by
    change T (D w v) = _
    rw [hD w v]
    rfl
  have hFeq (w : E) : F w = T ((hf w).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ)) := rfl
  have hFP (w : E) : HasFDerivAt F (DP w) w := by
    have he : F = fun u => T ((hf u).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ)) := funext hFeq
    rw [he]
    exact T.hasFDerivAt.comp w (hDiff w)
  have hPB (w : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) : ‖DP w‖ ≤ M₁ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ hM₁.le
    intro v
    change ‖J (D w v)‖ ≤ M₁*‖v‖
    rw [J.norm_map]
    exact ((D w).le_opNorm v).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hBound w hw) (norm_nonneg v))
  have hPL (w u : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) :
      ‖DP w-DP u‖ ≤ M₂*‖w-u‖ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (mul_nonneg hM₂.le (norm_nonneg _))
    intro v
    change ‖T (D w v)-T (D u v)‖ ≤ (M₂*‖w-u‖)*‖v‖
    rw [← map_sub]
    change ‖J ((D w-D u) v)‖ ≤ (M₂*‖w-u‖)*‖v‖
    rw [J.norm_map]
    exact ((D w-D u).le_opNorm v).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hLip u w hu hw) (norm_nonneg v))
steps.detail: Literal excerpt. The local name D denotes the Gaussian-space derivative; DP is the final joint-space family denoted D in the statement.

steps.title: Identify the actual predictor class with the Bochner mean
steps.text: The Gaussian parameter-average theorem proves scalar-section and Bochner integrability and identifies the predictor class in \(H_0\). Pull this class through \(J\) and commute the continuous linear map with the Bochner integral. This proves integrability of \(F|_S\) and identifies \(m_\rho\) with the actual predictor class in \(H\).
steps.lean:
let label : Lp ℝ 2 P := hlabel.toLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2)
  let K : S → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w => F w.1
  let mean : Measure S → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun μ => ∫ w, K w ∂μ
  obtain ⟨hfS,hcont,havg⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialAveraging.gaussian_polynomial_parameter_average_L2 (E := E) p
  have hKint (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) : Integrable K μ := by
    exact T.integrable_comp (havg μ hμ).2.1
  have hMeanClass (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      ∃ hpred : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) 2 P,
        hpred.toLp (fun z => predictor μ z.1) = mean μ := by
    obtain ⟨hscalar,hint,hmean,hident⟩ := havg μ hμ
    let hpred : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) 2 P :=
      hmean.comp_measurePreserving hmarg
    refine ⟨hpred,?_⟩
    calc
      hpred.toLp (fun z => predictor μ z.1) = T (hmean.toLp (predictor μ)) := rfl
      _ = T (∫ w, (hfS w).toLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w.1,x⟫_ℝ) ∂μ) := congrArg T hident
      _ = mean μ := (T.integral_comp_comm hint).symm

steps.title: Recover the literal potential from the residual class
steps.text: The class \(m_\rho-\ell\) has representative \(a_\rho(x)-y\) almost everywhere. Both this residual and the feature belong to \(L^2(P)\); Cauchy–Schwarz makes their product integrable. The \(L^2\) inner-product formula therefore turns the literal scalar potential into the displayed inner product for every ambient \(w\). The equality is a function identity in the weight variable.
steps.lean:
have hMeanAE (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      (fun z => mean μ z) =ᵐ[P] (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1) := by
    obtain ⟨hpred,hident⟩ := hMeanClass μ hμ
    rw [← hident]
    exact hpred.coeFn_toLp
  have hResidual (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      (fun z => (mean μ-label) z) =ᵐ[P] (fun z : E × ℝ => predictor μ z.1-z.2) := by
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_sub (mean μ) label,hMeanAE μ hμ,hlabel.coeFn_toLp]
      with z hs hm hy
    simp only [Pi.sub_apply] at hs
    rw [hs,hm,hy]
  have hPot (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) :
      V μ = fun w => 2 * ⟪mean μ-label,F w⟫_ℝ := by
    funext w
    change 2 * (∫ z, (predictor μ z.1-z.2)*p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P) = _
    rw [L2.inner_def]
    congr 1
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [hResidual μ hμ,(hfP w).coeFn_toLp] with z hr hw
    change F w z = p.eval ⟪w,z.1⟫_ℝ at hw
    simp only [Real.inner_apply,hr,hw]
steps.detail: Literal class and potential-identity excerpt. The scalar product integrability is delivered by MemLp.integrable_mul in the final assembly shown in step 6.

steps.title: Use the adjoint to identify the ambient gradient
steps.text: Fix the residual \(r=m_\rho-\ell\). Apply the existing quadratic-feature derivative theorem to \(w\mapsto2\langle r,F(w)\rangle_H\). For every direction \(v\), the adjoint converts its derivative to an inner product with \(2D(w)^*r\). The gradient–Fréchet derivative equivalence and the potential identity establish this actual ambient gradient at every \(w\).
steps.lean:
have hTangent :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureTangentGradient.quadratic_feature_potential_tangent_gradient
      F DP hFP M₁ M₂ hM₁.le hM₂.le hPB hPL
  have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (hμ : IsProbabilityMeasure μ) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label)) w := by
    rw [hPot μ hμ,hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt]
    have he : InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • (DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label)) =
        (2 : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ ((DP w).adjoint (mean μ-label)) := by
      ext v
      simp [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply,innerSL_apply_apply]
    rw [he]
    exact hTangent.1 (mean μ-label) w

steps.title: Substitute the gradient into the sphere projection
steps.text: For unit \(w\), subtract the normal component of the actual gradient. Substituting the identity from step 5 and distributing the scalar factor gives the required projection formula. Assemble the integrability and class identities already obtained, retaining the same operator family and constants for every probability law.
steps.formula: G_\rho(w)=2D(w)^*r-\langle2D(w)^*r,w\rangle w=2\bigl(D(w)^*r-\langle D(w)^*r,w\rangle w\bigr),\qquad r=m_\rho-\ell,\quad w\in S.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨hfP,hdfP,DP,M₁,M₂,hM₁,hM₂,hDP,hFP,hPB,hPL,?_⟩
  intro μ hμ
  refine ⟨(havg μ hμ).1,hKint μ hμ,hMeanClass μ hμ,hPot μ hμ,?_,?_⟩
  · intro w
    obtain ⟨hpred,hident⟩ := hMeanClass μ hμ
    exact ⟨(hpred.sub hlabel).integrable_mul (hfP w),hGrad μ hμ w,(hGrad μ hμ w).gradient⟩
  · intro w
    change gradient (V μ) w.1 - ⟪gradient (V μ) w.1,w.1⟫_ℝ • w.1 = _
    rw [(hGrad μ hμ w.1).gradient]
    simp only [smul_sub,real_inner_smul_left,smul_smul]
    rfl
